title: WhatToLookAt: learned relations become a sensing budget
summary: WhatToLookAt takes the history-written relation machinery from SighImageFactorization and asks a compressed-sensing-style engineering question: if useful structure is already known, where can future sensing or computation be omitted? Gates 0–8 establish the synthetic sensing-budget mechanism and sparse-measurement geometry. The practical SDXL branch then tests the same principle on real GPU computation: naive independent crop refinement fails, but cheap edge evidence still localizes where the full-frame diffusion update matters, and a globally coherent masked diffusion trajectory converts that cue into a causal improvement.

nodes.claim: Learns persistent relations from past temporal structure and uses them as a prior for future sparse sensing; local relation uncertainty withdraws sharing authority and purchases extra measurements only where confidence is low.
nodes.survived: Learned relations can replace future observations in controlled worlds; local evidence can buy measurements selectively; sparse measurement geometry and coded overlap matter; and the practical SDXL branch shows the same abstract rule survives outside the synthetic world: edge-selected 4/16 regions contain much more future refinement activity than random, and when one global diffusion trajectory is preserved those regions recover 30.87% of the full teacher correction versus 17.30% for matched random masks. The P2 lesson is therefore specifically about sparse causal authority inside a globally coherent computation, not about naively cutting the computation into independent spatial subgraphs. The practical survivor is now narrowly defined: cheap spatial evidence predicts where a globally coherent diffusion update matters, but that information has not yet been converted into a quality-preserving speedup at 512×512 SDXL-Turbo. The final 512px profiler shows why: VAE encode+decode consumes 58.36% of the ordinary stage while both U-Net calls together consume 31.24%, so the dominant bottleneck is outside the routed operation. The 512px closeout identifies a conventional engineering default rather than a new routing mechanism: sdxl-vae-fp16-fix preserves ~99.5–99.7% of the standard-VAE continuation while giving ~1.36–1.38× full-stage speedup on the RTX 3060. The high-resolution question remains viable only under overlap-blended tile assembly, where skipping a call fades back to the smooth base rather than creating a hard block.
nodes.killed: Blind trust, shuffled confidence, coordinate memory and equal-cost random extra reads fail matched controls. Extreme row sparsity, one-hit coverage, and degree-2 overlap are insufficient in the synthetic chain. In the practical branch, globally refining the Sihti core does not accelerate SDXL, Sihti residue is not the best compute router, and independent crop diffusion is actively harmful and slower; local routing only becomes valid when the actuator preserves the shared global denoising state. P3 additionally kills hard spatial U-Net execution on this SDXL-Turbo/RTX-3060 route: 25%, 56.25%, and even 100%-naive-spatial-work crop decompositions all have negative correction recovery and are slower than the full-frame teacher. P4 then shows that established DeepCache can shave about 0.10–0.11 s from the four-step 512px stage, but none of the tested cache branches preserves the preregistered quality frontier, so no adaptive-cache mechanism is earned at this scale. The 512×512 Turbo acceleration search is now closed: hard spatial U-Net sparsity fails, tested DeepCache misses the quality frontier, and the only passing speed improvement comes from replacing the dominant VAE bottleneck rather than from WhatToLookAt routing. The first high-resolution H0 hard-paste design is invalid as visual evidence because the all-tile teacher itself contained obvious rectangular seams; the flaw was caught from the contact sheet before scoring.

edges.why: WhatToLookAt explicitly states that it pushes the compressed-sensing question into the SighImageFactorization/Sihti lineage and operationalizes SighImageFactorization's learned relation state as a prior that can reduce future sensing.

WhatToLookAt explicitly names Sihti in its lineage and carries forward the operator-dependent-structure framing, but does not claim Sihti code inheritance; the new currency is measurement cost rather than residue location.
